en: Which bus goes to the railway station?
explain: Use 'which' when there are a few choices. 'Goes to' shows the place the bus is going.

alt.en: Does this bus go to the railway station?

en: The train is running twenty minutes late.
context: Telling a friend about a delay.
explain: 'Is running late' is a common way to say the train is delayed right now.

en: Please drop me at the main gate.
tamil: தயவுசெஞ்சு என்னை மெயின் கேட்டில் இறக்கி விடுங்க.
context: Telling an auto driver where to stop.
explain: 'Please' makes the request polite. 'Drop me' means let me get down.

en: How much will you charge to the airport?
context: Asking an auto or cab driver the price.
explain: 'Will' is used to ask about a price you will pay. 'Charge' means ask money for a service.

en: I booked two tickets for tomorrow morning.
tamil: நாளைக்கு காலைக்கு ரெண்டு டிக்கெட் புக் பண்ணிட்டேன்.
explain: 'Booked' is the past form of 'book'. It shows the action is finished.

en: Could you show me the way to the bus stand?
explain: 'Could you' is a polite way to ask for help. 'The way to' is used with directions.

en: Keep going straight, then turn left at the signal.
tamil: நேரா போயிட்டே இருங்க, அப்புறம் சிக்னலில் இடது பக்கம் திரும்புங்க.
explain: Directions use simple commands like 'go' and 'turn'. 'At the signal' tells the place.

alt.en: Turn left at the signal after you go straight.
alt.tamil: நேரா போனதுக்கு அப்புறம் சிக்னலில் இடது பக்கம் திரும்புங்க.

en: My flight has been cancelled.
context: Calling home or the office from the airport.
explain: 'Has been cancelled' tells us something happened and the result matters now.

en: I don't have a window seat.
explain: 'Don't have' makes the sentence negative. Use 'a' before a single seat.

en: Is there a hotel near the beach?
context: Asking a local while planning a trip.
explain: 'Is there' asks if something exists. 'Near' shows it is close by.

en: We will reach Madurai by six in the morning.
tamil: நாங்க காலைல ஆறு மணிக்கு மதுரை போய் சேருவோம்.
explain: 'By six' means at or before six. 'Will reach' is for a plan or expectation.

en: Can I get a refund for this ticket?
explain: 'Can I' asks for permission or a possibility. 'Refund' means getting your money back.

en: I missed the last bus yesterday.
context: Explaining why you were late or stuck.
explain: 'Missed' is the past of 'miss'. We say 'miss the bus' when we are late for it.

en: The platform number has not been announced yet.
explain: 'Has not been announced yet' shows something is still waiting to happen.

en: Please keep your luggage with you.
context: Advice at a station or airport.
explain: 'Keep' is a simple command. 'Luggage' is never used as 'luggages'.

en: What time does the next train leave?
explain: Use 'does' with 'the next train'. After 'does' the verb stays simple: 'leave'.

alt.en: When is the next train leaving?

en: I am waiting at the bus stop right now.
context: Replying to a friend on the phone.
explain: 'Am waiting' shows the action is happening now. 'Right now' adds emphasis.

en: The traffic was terrible this morning.
tamil: இன்னைக்கு காலைல டிராஃபிக் ரொம்ப மோசமா இருந்துச்சு.
explain: 'Was' is used with a single thing like 'traffic'. 'Terrible' means very bad.

en: Do you have a room with air conditioning?
explain: 'Do you have' is a simple way to ask if something is available.

en: Please wake me up when we reach Salem.
context: Asking a co-passenger on an overnight journey.
explain: 'Wake me up' means make me awake. 'When we reach' uses present for a future time.

en: I won't take an auto in this rain.
tamil: இந்த மழைல நான் ஆட்டோ எடுக்க மாட்டேன்.
explain: 'Won't' means will not. It shows a decision about the future.
